transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, I hope I'm not overreacting by being here, it's probably just normal stress, but... well, I came in because I've been having a little trouble lately. 

I'm an artist, and I was working on a memorial piece for my aunt recently, and... I just kept getting these really awful, unwanted thoughts. I don't want you to think I'm crazy or anything, but I kept worrying that I was going to dishonor her somehow? Like, if I made one wrong photo placement or picked the wrong color, it would mean I didn't love her enough. 

I know it sounds a bit silly out loud, but I just couldn't brush them off like my normal creative doubts. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this the right way.

When you had these troubling thoughts about dishonoring your aunt, did you feel driven to do something repeatedly—like checking, adjusting, or redoing parts of your work—to try to ease the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Um, well... yes, I suppose so. I mean, as an artist, you always want things to look right, so I usually just tell myself I'm being thorough, you know? But... yeah, if I'm being completely honest, I do get a little stuck sometimes. 

I'll end up, um, rereading the label text for the piece over and over again. Or I'll find myself just nudging the same objects on my work table, and checking the layout photos repeatedly. I just... I have to keep doing it until it finally feels 'settled,' I guess? Even though part of me completely knows it’s already fine and I don't need to touch it. 

It's actually a bit embarrassing to admit out loud, because I know I’m just losing valuable studio time when I do it. Is that the kind of thing you meant? I want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do these thoughts and behaviors interfere with your ability to work, spend time with loved ones, or enjoy life the way you used to?

Um, well, I wouldn't say it's completely ruining my life or anything dramatic like that. I'm still getting most of my work done, and I definitely still enjoy my art! I don't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything. 

But... I guess it has gotten a little in the way recently. Like, because of all the extra time I end up losing in the studio when I get stuck on those details, I actually ended up missing a deadline for a grant application. And... well, I also backed out of a gallery talk that I really, really wanted to do, just because I felt so behind and stressed. 

I'm trying my best to manage it, though! Does that sound like a normal amount of interference, or... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Do you ever have thoughts that come into your mind that you can’t seem to get rid of, even though you know they might not make sense? And when you have those thoughts, do you feel like you have to do something over and over again to try to neutralize them or prevent something bad from happening?

Um, well... I think I actually just mentioned that, right? With the memorial piece for my aunt, and having to check the labels and the photos over and over? 

I hope I didn't misunderstand your question earlier! But yes, that's exactly it. The thoughts about dishonoring her just kind of pop up and stick there, even though I know they're a bit irrational. And then I do the checking and the adjusting to make the feeling go away, like I was saying before. 

I don't really have any other thoughts or behaviors like that, though. It's really just been with this one project. I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. Am I doing okay?
Have you noticed these kinds of thoughts or behaviors happening in other areas of your life, or is this something that only happens when you're working on this memorial piece for your aunt?

Um, no, it really is just this one specific memorial piece. I haven't noticed anything like that happening anywhere else at all. My other art projects are completely fine, and, you know, my day-to-day life is totally normal. 

I really try to keep things running smoothly, so I'm not, like, a burden or causing problems for anyone. It's just this one very personal project that's kind of... tripping me up a little bit right now. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough for you, I just want to make sure you have everything you need.
Outside of your concerns about the memorial piece, have you ever experienced any intrusive thoughts, urges, or images that cause you significant anxiety or distress?

Um, no, definitely not. I really don't have anything like that outside of this one project. Like I said, I'm usually very put together! I don't have, like, weird or disturbing thoughts popping into my head or anything like that. 

I'm a pretty positive person, honestly! I like to focus on the good things, and I really try not to let myself get bogged down by negativity or anxiety in my normal life. 

So, no, nothing else like that at all. I hope that's okay? I just want to reassure you that I'm generally doing really well, aside from this one little hiccup with my aunt's piece. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for?

Do you ever feel anxious or stressed about making mistakes or being responsible for something bad happening, even in regular everyday situations outside of your art, like forgetting to lock the door or turning off the stove?

Oh, um, no, not really. I mean, I think I'm just... normally responsible? Like, I'll lock the door when I leave, of course, but I don't sit around stressing that I left the stove on or worrying that something terrible is going to happen because of me. 

I'm actually very organized with my daily routine, so I just... I try to do things right the first time, I guess. I don't get anxious about everyday chores or anything like that at all. 

I hope that's a helpful answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult, it's just really only that one art piece that's been bothering me. Am I doing okay with these questions?

When you're working on the memorial piece, do you find yourself doing anything else—like silently repeating certain words, phrases, or numbers in your head—to try to reduce the anxiety or make things feel 'right'?

Um... well, I don't really do the repeating words or numbers thing. That sounds... a little intense, honestly. I just... I do have a few little habits, I guess you could call them? Just to make sure everything is perfect for her. 

Like, sometimes I'll... I'll end up rereading the text for the label a few times, just to be absolutely sure there are no typos. And I might, you know, nudge the objects on the table just a tiny bit, or check the layout photos again. I just do it over and over until it finally feels... settled, I guess? 

I mean, part of me knows it's already fine, and I'm probably just wasting my studio time, but... I just want it to be right. It's not a big deal or anything, just a little quirk I have with this one project. Does that sound okay? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I just want to be totally honest with you.

Do the intrusive thoughts about dishonoring your aunt ever cause you intense anxiety or distress simply because of what the thoughts themselves mean to you, even when you’re not working on the memorial piece?

Oh, um... no. Not really. When I'm not in the studio working on it, I'm... I'm usually completely fine! 

Like I mentioned earlier, I really try to keep a positive mindset. I don't sit around agonizing over what those worries mean about me as a person or anything like that. It's really just when I'm right there, looking at the piece, wanting to make sure it's perfect for her. Once I step away and go about my day, I can pretty much leave it behind me. 

I hope that makes sense? I really don't want you to think I'm, like, agonizing over this all day long, because I'm actually managing my day-to-day life really well, I promise. Does that help answer your question?

When you're working on the memorial piece and having those intrusive thoughts about dishonoring your aunt, does the thought itself upset you so much that you feel intense anxiety, even before you start checking or adjusting things?

Um... no, not really. I don't think so? Like, the thoughts themselves don't make me panic or anything like that. 

It's more just... a fleeting feeling, I guess? Like a little reminder popping up that says, "Hey, make sure this is right." It doesn't send me into a spiral of intense anxiety or make me feel awful before I even touch the piece. I just... I see something that might need a tiny adjustment, and I fix it, and that's it. 

I'm really trying to keep things in perspective, you know? I know it's just an art project, even if it is a special one. So I promise I'm not standing there trembling with anxiety over a thought. I'm handling it pretty well, I think. Is that... is that the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I'm doing.
